Soil Biodiversity Under Organic Management

Introduction

Species richness in temperate cropland has been studied for decades, and the
picture is not settled. Organic management increased soil invertebrate species
richness by about 31 percent (Smith, 2019). The same paired-fields design was
later repeated at a larger scale (Jones & Patel, 2020).

Results

The magnitude of the richness effect depended strongly on the baseline soil
carbon of each field (Smith, 2019). Earthworm biomass responded faster than
species counts, which complicates any single-metric summary of soil health.
Reported effects on microbial diversity were smaller and less consistent
(Smith, 2019).

Discussion

These findings matter for policy because subsidy schemes increasingly reward
measurable biodiversity outcomes. Nothing in the present data speaks to
tropical systems at all.

References

Smith, J. (2019). Organic Management and Soil Life. Journal of Soil Biology.
Jones, A., & Patel, R. (2020). Paired Fields. Agronomy Reports.
